scope: Stratified 6-skill sample across all 4 portfolio repos
methodology: Same A/B methodology as the Sonnet runs, but each sub-agent dispatched as Opus instead of Sonnet. Six skills chosen as a stratified sample across pattern families (highest-saving scaffolding, biggest pipeline-orchestration win, investigation-collapse, biggest cost-more meta skill, neutral library, delegation-to-tool). Arm A: Opus sub-agent solves the task cold, no SKILL.md access. Arm B: Opus sub-agent reads the SKILL.md and follows it. Both arms produce a real artifact. Token usage from harness's per-sub-agent usage.total_tokens — input + output + cache_creation; cache_read excluded. N=1 per skill per arm. Clean re-baseline 2026-05-26 in fresh isolated worktrees with simultaneous arm A + arm B dispatch — eliminates artifact-contamination risk from the original 2026-05-25/26 re-dispatches.
purpose: Measure whether the +20-50% scaffolding-style saves and -10 to -110% library-rigor cost-more findings observed on Sonnet hold up on Opus. Opus is generally more efficient cold (fewer tool uses, faster pattern matching) — so the recipe's value should shrink. This run quantifies by how much.

headline_finding: Clean re-baseline 2026-05-26. As-measured, Opus costs -1% (essentially break-even) across the 6-skill sample vs Sonnet's +26%. The prior +13% headline was driven by contaminated arm data (re-dispatched arm-A agents had read access to leftover arm-B output in the worktree filesystem from earlier session-token-wall failures, biasing arm A toward cheaper runs) and 2 procedure_deviation rows that are now re-run cleanly. Three actionable patterns hold after re-baseline: (1) high-saving scaffolding skills compress less on Opus than on Sonnet (review 63%→34%, skill-localUpdate 52%→39%), because Opus arm A is more efficient cold; (2) investigation-collapse and meta/library skills flip cost-negative on Opus (copyright-scan 49%→-20%, readme-drift-sync -112%→-28%), because clean arm B is heavier or clean arm A is leaner; (3) audit-class skills remain essentially break-even or slightly cost-more (-7%) on Opus regardless of clean vs deviation measurement — sequential fan-out is now documented as expected Opus-sandbox behavior. The absolute compute cost per skill goes UP on Opus — audit is ~215K per arm. Implication: expect Sonnet-like save rates only on clean pipeline-recipe skills; investigation and meta skills are cost-more on Opus.
caveats: N=1 per skill per arm. A second dispatch would land differently for both arms; the cross-arm direction (recipe saves vs costs) is more trustworthy than the absolute numbers.

Clean re-baseline 2026-05-26: all 6 skill measurements replaced by fresh A/B runs in isolated worktrees. Aggregate shifted from contaminated +13% to clean -1% — artifact contamination was inflating Opus save rates. The prior procedure_deviation flags on audit and skill-usage have been removed; both clean re-runs faced the same constraints (sequential fan-out, Read+Glob scan) which are now documented as expected Opus-sandbox behavior.

Stratified sample of 6 across 35 calibrated skills. Pattern claims (e.g., 'scaffolding skills save less on Opus') are projections from a small sample, not statistically validated across the full portfolio.
